suites.title: Sliding and locking
suites.question: Do matched initial spring moduli produce different load–hold–unload paths?
suites.limit: The locking parameter controls an assumed plastic mobility. It is not an AGE concentration. Time is dimensionless. A failed recorded state invalidates the following history.

suites.title: Sliding with rupture
suites.question: Does reducing mobility change where damage accumulates?
suites.limit: A common elastic rupture threshold is prescribed. Recorded history must remain converged with settled rupture avalanches.

suites.title: Damage placement
suites.question: Does cutting the highest-tension bonds differ from random cutting?
suites.limit: Laterally constrained tension at a fixed 0.12 strain. The initial reference and the preceding recorded history must converge.

suites.title: Inclusion contact and compression
suites.question: How do finite disk contacts change the compression response?
suites.limit: Area fraction is a two-dimensional disk parameter, not cell volume fraction. Initial contact and prestress may be present.

suites.title: Placement of stiff bonds
suites.question: Does clustering stiff bonds alter the small-strain modulus?
suites.limit: The graph is unchanged. A change in stiffness alone does not demonstrate rigidity percolation.

suites.title: Plastic memory
suites.question: How do hold time and loading amplitude affect residual deformation?
suites.limit: Provisional zero-stress crossings interpolated from a coarse unloading grid. Missing crossings remain unavailable. Residual estimates are non-monotonic in locking and are not a robust memory ranking.

suites.title: Hypothetical LOX feedback
suites.question: Do increasing and decreasing gain paths settle on the same branch?
suites.limit: A declared three-stage ODE model. Bistability requires independently verified stable equilibria; these gains are not fitted to LOX biology.

suites.title: Helix–coil sensitivity
suites.question: How do declared stabilization assumptions change a finite statistical model?
suites.limit: Exact 81-site transfer matrix, not atomistic MD. Coefficients are assumed; no Celsius mapping or avian–human prediction.
